pharm: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor; potent, selective blocker of presynaptic serotonin (5-HT) reuptake

summary: Sertraline is an SSRI antidepressant used for major depressive disorder, OCD, panic disorder, PTSD, social anxiety disorder, and PMDD. It is started at 50 mg once daily (25 mg in panic, PTSD, and certain pediatric/PMDD scenarios) and titrated up to a maximum of 200 mg/day. It carries a boxed warning for increased suicidality in children, adolescents, and young adults, is contraindicated with MAOIs because of serotonin syndrome risk, and should be tapered rather than stopped abruptly to limit discontinuation symptoms.
indications: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) in adults and pediatric patients ages 6-17
Panic disorder in adults, with or without agoraphobia
Social anxiety disorder (social phobia) in adults

admin: Administer once daily, in the morning or evening, with or without food
Make dose changes no more frequently than once a week given the ~24 hour half-life
Oral solution must be diluted before use per product labeling; tablet and solution are approximately bioequivalent
Allow at least 14 days between stopping an MAOI and starting sertraline, and at least 14 days after stopping sertraline before starting an MAOI
Taper gradually rather than stopping abruptly to limit discontinuation symptoms
moa: Potently and selectively inhibits reuptake of serotonin (5-HT) into presynaptic neurons, increasing synaptic serotonin availability. It has only weak effects on norepinephrine and dopamine reuptake and negligible affinity for adrenergic, cholinergic, GABA, dopaminergic, histaminergic, serotonergic, or benzodiazepine receptors, and does not inhibit monoamine oxidase.

absolute: Concomitant use of MAOIs intended to treat psychiatric disorders, or within 14 days of stopping such an MAOI (serotonin syndrome risk)
Starting sertraline in a patient treated with linezolid or intravenous methylene blue
Hypersensitivity to sertraline or any inactive ingredient
relative: Other serotonergic drugs (triptans, TCAs, fentanyl, lithium, tramadol, tryptophan, buspirone, St. John's Wort)
History of mania/bipolar disorder (screen before treatment)
monitor: Suicidality, clinical worsening, and behavior changes especially early and at dose changes
Prothrombin time/INR when starting or stopping in warfarin patients

preg: No adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women (former Pregnancy Category C); use only if potential benefit justifies potential risk. Third-trimester exposure has been associated with neonatal complications (respiratory distress, cyanosis, apnea, seizures, temperature instability, feeding difficulty, hypoglycemia, hypotonia/hypertonia, tremor, jitteriness, irritability) and a possible increased risk of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN). Weigh against risk of untreated depression, which may relapse if antidepressants are discontinued.
lact: It is not known whether, and if so in what amount, sertraline or its metabolites are excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk, exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman and monitor the infant.
renal: Sertraline is extensively metabolized with only minor urinary excretion of unchanged drug; multiple-dose pharmacokinetics were unaltered across mild, moderate-to-severe, and hemodialysis-dependent renal impairment. No dosage adjustment is needed for renal impairment.
hepatic: Liver impairment reduces sertraline clearance; mild impairment gave roughly 3-fold greater sertraline exposure. Use a lower or less frequent dose and approach with caution. Effects in moderate and severe hepatic impairment have not been studied.

major: MAOIs (psychiatric, plus linezolid and intravenous methylene blue) - contraindicated, serotonin syndrome
Other serotonergic agents - triptans, TCAs, fentanyl, lithium, tramadol, tryptophan, buspirone, St. John's Wort (serotonin syndrome)
Warfarin and drugs affecting hemostasis - increased prothrombin time and bleeding risk
moderate: CYP2D6 substrates with narrow index - TCAs, propafenone, flecainide (sertraline may raise their levels)
minor: CYP3A4 substrates - carbamazepine, terfenadine, cisapride (no clinically significant inhibition)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food slightly increases AUC and raises Cmax by about 25% with a shorter time to peak
interactions.alcohol: Concomitant use of sertraline and alcohol is not recommended
interactions.diagnostics: May prolong prothrombin time/INR with warfarin; associated with small mean increases in total cholesterol (~3%) and triglycerides (~5%), and a small decrease in serum uric acid (~7%); may cause asymptomatic transaminase elevations and hyponatremia

rare: Severe cutaneous reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome
emergency: Serotonin syndrome (agitation, hyperthermia, autonomic instability, rigidity, myoclonus, seizures)
Emergent suicidality or marked clinical worsening

monitoring: Suicidality, clinical worsening, agitation, and behavior changes, especially in the first few months and at dose changes
Signs of serotonin syndrome, particularly with other serotonergic drugs
Serum sodium in elderly or volume-depleted patients (hyponatremia)
Prothrombin time/INR when initiating or discontinuing sertraline in patients on warfarin
Discontinuation symptoms during dose reduction or stopping
Weight and growth in pediatric patients on long-term therapy
Screen for bipolar disorder before starting an antidepressant
counsel: Watch for and immediately report worsening mood, agitation, or thoughts of self-harm, especially early in treatment or after dose changes
Do not stop abruptly; discontinuation can cause withdrawal-like symptoms, so taper under guidance
Avoid MAOIs and tell your clinician about all serotonergic medicines, supplements, and St. John's Wort
Seek care for agitation, fever, sweating, shivering, racing heart, muscle stiffness, or twitching (serotonin syndrome)
Use caution combining with NSAIDs, aspirin, or blood thinners due to bleeding risk
Do not drink alcohol while taking sertraline
Tell your clinician if you are pregnant, planning pregnancy, or breastfeeding
pk: Antidepressant/anxiolytic effect typically over 2-4 weeks; steady state in ~1 week
Plasma Cmax at about 4.5-8.4 hours after dosing
pearls: Start panic disorder, PTSD, and social anxiety disorder at 25 mg/day to reduce early activation, then increase to 50 mg after one week
PMDD can be dosed continuously (up to 150 mg/day) or only in the luteal phase (up to 100 mg/day, with a 50 mg 3-day titration step when using 100 mg)
Among the SSRIs least likely to cause clinically significant CYP2D6 inhibition at lower doses, but still monitor narrow-index 2D6 substrates
MDD is not approved in pediatric patients; only OCD (ages 6-17) is an approved pediatric indication
Monitor INR closely with warfarin and counsel on bleeding risk with NSAIDs/aspirin
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular once-daily schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Signs include somnolence, vomiting, tachycardia, nausea, dizziness, agitation, and tremor; severe cases may show bradycardia, bundle branch block, QT prolongation, coma, convulsions, delirium, hallucinations, hypotension or hypertension, serotonin syndrome, pancreatitis, and syncope. Management is supportive: secure airway, oxygenation, and ventilation, monitor cardiac rhythm and vital signs, and give activated charcoal; gastric lavage may help if performed soon after ingestion. Do not induce emesis; forced diuresis, dialysis, hemoperfusion, and exchange transfusion are unlikely to help given the large volume of distribution. There is no specific antidote; consider multiple-drug involvement and contact a poison control center.
